questions.question: If A = 1 - 10 + 3 - 12 + 5 - 14 + 7 + … up to 60 terms, then what is the value of A?
questions.questionHtml: If A = 1 - 10 + 3 - 12 + 5 - 14 + 7 + … up to 60 terms, then what is the value of A?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Group the series into pairs: (1 − 10) + (3 − 12) + (5 − 14) + …

Sum of each pair = −9

Total terms = 60 ⇒ Total pairs = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 pairs

Total sum A = 30 × (−9) = −270

∴ The correct answer is -270.

Alternate Method

Given: A = 1 − 10 + 3 − 12 + 5 − 14 + … up to 60 terms

Separate the series into two Arithmetic Progressions (APs) of 30 terms each:

AP1: 1, 3, 5, 7, … (Odd positioned terms)

AP2: −10, −12, −14, −16, … (Even positioned terms)

Formula for Sum of AP: Sn = (n ÷ 2) × [2a + (n − 1)d]

⇒ For AP1: a = 1, d = 2, n = 30

⇒ S1 = (30 ÷ 2) × [2(1) + (30 − 1) × 2] = 15 × [2 + 58] = 15 × 60 = 900

⇒ For AP2: a = −10, d = −2, n = 30

⇒ S2 = (30 ÷ 2) × [2(−10) + (30 − 1) × (−2)] = 15 × [−20 − 58] = 15 × (−78) = −1170

⇒ Total Sum A = S1 + S2 = 900 + (−1170) = −270

∴ The correct answer is -270.

Additional Information

Sum of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

The sum of first n terms is Sn = (n ÷ 2)[2a + (n − 1)d] or Sn = (n ÷ 2)[a + l], where l is the last term.

General Term of AP

The n-th term of an AP is given by an = a + (n − 1)d.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n odd natural numbers (1, 3, 5, …) is always n2.

Sum of First n Even Numbers

The sum of the first n even natural numbers (2, 4, 6, …) is given by n(n + 1).

questions.question: How many natural numbers are there between 1000 and 2000, which when divided by 341 leaves remainder 5?
questions.questionHtml: How many natural numbers are there between 1000 and 2000, which when divided by 341 leaves remainder 5?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

General form of the number: N = 341k + 5 (where k is an integer).

Estimate k by dividing bounds: 1000 ÷ 341 ≈ 2.93 and 2000 ÷ 341 ≈ 5.86.

Integers k between 2.93 and 5.86 are 3, 4, and 5.

Total count of such numbers = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Divisor = 341

Remainder = 5

Range = 1000 < N < 2000

Formula Used:

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

Calculations:

Any natural number which when divided by 341 leaves remainder 5 is of the form N = 341k + 5.

According to the condition:

⇒ 1000 < 341k + 5 < 2000

Subtracting 5 from all sides:

⇒ 1000 − 5 < 341k < 2000 − 5

⇒ 995 < 341k < 1995

Dividing by 341:

⇒ 995 ÷ 341 < k < 1995 ÷ 341

⇒ 2.917 < k < 5.850

Since k must be a natural number, the possible values for k are:

⇒ k = 3, 4, 5

Calculating the numbers:

⇒ For k = 3: N = 341 × 3 + 5 = 1023 + 5 = 1028

⇒ For k = 4: N = 341 × 4 + 5 = 1364 + 5 = 1369

⇒ For k = 5: N = 341 × 5 + 5 = 1705 + 5 = 1710

∴ There are 3 such numbers.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Euclid Division Lemma

It states that for any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

Arithmetic Progression in Remainders

Numbers that leave the same remainder when divided by a constant d form an AP with a common difference d. Example: N = dk + r.

Finding Number of Terms

To find the number of terms in an AP within a range, use n = [(Last Term − First Term) ÷ d] + 1.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE? I. (0.7) 2 + (0.07) 2 + (11.1) 2 > 123.8 II. (1.12) 2 + (10.3) 2 + (1.05) 2 > 108.3

I. (0.7)2 + (0.07)2 + (11.1)2 > 123.8

II. (1.12)2 + (10.3)2 + (1.05)2 > 108.3

II. (1.12)2 + (10.3)2 + (1.05)2 > 108.3

⇒ (11.1)2 = 123.21

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE? \({\rm{I}}.\frac{1}{{1 \times 3}} + \frac{1}{{3 \times 5}} + \frac{1}{{5 \times 7}} + \ldots + \frac{1}{{11 \times 13}} = \frac{{12}}{{13}}\) \({\rm{II}}.\frac{1}{{1 \times 2}} + \frac{1}{{2 \times 3}} + \frac{1}{{3 \times 4}} + \ldots + \frac{1}{{12 \times 13}} = \frac{{12}}{{13}}\)
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

\({\rm{I}}.\frac{1}{{1 \times 3}} + \frac{1}{{3 \times 5}} + \frac{1}{{5 \times 7}} + \ldots + \frac{1}{{11 \times 13}} = \frac{{12}}{{13}}\)

\({\rm{II}}.\frac{1}{{1 \times 2}} + \frac{1}{{2 \times 3}} + \frac{1}{{3 \times 4}} + \ldots + \frac{1}{{12 \times 13}} = \frac{{12}}{{13}}\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a series of type 1/(a × b) + 1/(b × c) + ..., Sum = (1 / Difference) × [(1 / First Term) − (1 / Last Term)].

Statement I: Difference = 2, First = 1, Last = 13. Sum = (1/2) × [1 − (1/13)] = (1/2) × (12/13) = 6/13. (False)

Statement II: Difference = 1, First = 1, Last = 13. Sum = (1/1) × [1 − (1/13)] = 12/13. (True)

∴ The correct answer is Only II.

Alternate Method

Given Statements:

I. 1/(1 × 3) + 1/(3 × 5) + 1/(5 × 7) + ... + 1/(11 × 13) = 12/13

II. 1/(1 × 2) + 1/(2 × 3) + 1/(3 × 4) + ... + 1/(12 × 13) = 12/13

Formula used: 1 / [n × (n + k)] = (1 / k) × [1/n − 1/(n + k)]

Checking Statement I:

⇒ Sum = 1/(1 × 3) + 1/(3 × 5) + ... + 1/(11 × 13)

⇒ Sum = (1/2) × [ (1/1 − 1/3) + (1/3 − 1/5) + ... + (1/11 − 1/13) ]

⇒ Sum = (1/2) × [ 1 − 1/13 ]

⇒ Sum = (1/2) × (12/13) = 6/13

⇒ 6/13 ≠ 12/13. Hence, Statement I is FALSE.

Checking Statement II:

⇒ Sum = 1/(1 × 2) + 1/(2 × 3) + ... + 1/(12 × 13)

⇒ Sum = (1/1 − 1/2) + (1/2 − 1/3) + ... + (1/12 − 1/13)

⇒ Sum = 1 − 1/13 = 12/13

⇒ 12/13 = 12/13. Hence, Statement II is TRUE.

∴ The correct answer is Only II.

Additional Information

Telescoping Series

A telescoping series is a series whose partial sums eventually only have a fixed number of terms after cancellation. The general form is Σ [f(n) − f(n+1)].

General Sum Formula

For a series with common difference 'd' in the denominator factors: Sum = (1/d) × [(1/First Factor) − (1/Last Factor)].

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is given by Sn = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE? I. 3/71 < 3/91 < 3/99 II. 13/135 > 12/135 > 11/135

Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

II. 13/135 > 12/135 > 11/135
questions.solution:
Given:

I. \(\frac{3}{71} < \frac{3}{91} < \frac{3}{99}\)

II. \(\frac{13}{135} > \frac{12}{135} > \frac{11}{135}\)

Formula used:

1. If numerators are same, the fraction with the smaller denominator is larger.

2. If denominators are same, the fraction with the larger numerator is larger.

Calculation:

For Statement I:

Numerators = 3

Comparing denominators: 71 < 91 < 99

⇒ \(\frac{3}{71} > \frac{3}{91} > \frac{3}{99}\)

Statement I is FALSE.

For Statement II:

Denominators = 135

Comparing numerators: 13 > 12 > 11

⇒ \(\frac{13}{135} > \frac{12}{135} > \frac{11}{135}\)

Statement II is TRUE.

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: If 1 + (1/2) + (1/3) + … + (1/20) = k, then what is the value of (1/4) + (1/6) + (1/8) + … + (1/40)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The target series is 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/8 + … + 1/40.

Factor out 1/2 from the series: 1/2 × (1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + … + 1/20).

The original sum is k = 1 + (1/2 + 1/3 + … + 1/20).

The term in the bracket is simply (k − 1).

Required value = 1/2 × (k − 1) = (k − 1)/2.

∴ The correct answer is (k − 1)/2.

Alternate Method

Given: 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + … + 1/20 = k

To Find: 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/8 + … + 1/40

⇒ Let S = 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/8 + … + 1/40

⇒ Taking 1/2 common from each term:

⇒ S = 1/2 × [ (1 × 1/2) + (1 × 1/3) + (1 × 1/4) + … + (1 × 1/20) ]

⇒ S = 1/2 × [ 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + … + 1/20 ]

⇒ From the given equation, 1 + (1/2 + 1/3 + … + 1/20) = k

⇒ Therefore, (1/2 + 1/3 + … + 1/20) = k − 1

⇒ Substituting this value back into the expression for S:

⇒ S = 1/2 × (k − 1)

⇒ S = (k − 1)/2

∴ The correct answer is (k − 1)/2.

Additional Information

Harmonic Series

A harmonic series is the sum of the reciprocals of terms in an arithmetic progression, typically expressed as ∑(1/n).

Distributive Property in Series

If a series is given by ∑ an = S, then the series ∑ (c × an) is equal to c × S, where c is a constant.

Manipulation of Summation Limits

To find a partial sum or a modified series, always relate the required terms back to the base series by adding or subtracting specific constants or coefficients.

questions.question: If A = 2 32 , B = 2 31 + 2 30 + 2 29 + … + 2 0 and C = 3 15 + 3 14 + 3 13 + … + 3 0 , then which of the following option is TRUE?
questions.questionHtml: If A = 2<sup>32</sup>, B = 2<sup>31</sup> + 2<sup>30</sup> + 2<sup>29</sup> + … + 2<sup>0</sup> and C = 3<sup>15</sup> + 3<sup>14</sup> + 3<sup>13</sup> + … + 3<sup>0</sup>, then which of the following option is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of powers of 2 from 20 to 2n−1 is always 2n − 1.

Therefore, B = 232 − 1. Since A = 232, it follows that A > B.

For C, the sum of powers of 3 is (316 − 1) ÷ 2.

Comparing B = 416 − 1 and C ≈ 0.5 × 316, it is clear that B > C.

∴ The correct answer is A > B > C.

Alternate Method

Given: A = 232, B = 231 + 230 + … + 20, C = 315 + 314 + … + 30

Formula for sum of GP: Sn = a(rn − 1) ÷ (r − 1)

⇒ For B: a = 1, r = 2, n = 32 terms

⇒ B = 1 × (232 − 1) ÷ (2 − 1) = 232 − 1

⇒ Since A = 232 and B = 232 − 1, then A > B

⇒ For C: a = 1, r = 3, n = 16 terms

⇒ C = 1 × (316 − 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = (316 − 1) ÷ 2

⇒ Expressing B with the same exponent: B = 232 − 1 = (22)16 − 1 = 416 − 1

⇒ Comparing B = 416 − 1 and C = (316 − 1) ÷ 2, clearly B > C as 416 > 316 and C is further reduced by half.

⇒ Combined relation: A > B > C

∴ The correct answer is A > B > C.

Additional Information

Sum of Geometric Progression

For a sequence a, ar, ar2, …, the sum of n terms is Sn = a(rn − 1) ÷ (r − 1) when r ≠ 1.

Power Comparison Rule

If x > y > 1 and n > 0, then xn > yn. This allows comparing expressions by equating their exponents.

Sum of Powers of 2

The sum of the first n powers of 2 (starting from 20) is always equal to the next power of 2 minus 1: ∑2i = 2n − 1.

questions.question: If x + y = 10 and xy = 4, then what is the value of x 4 + y 4 ?
questions.questionHtml: If x + y = 10 and xy = 4, then what is the value of x<sup>4</sup> + y<sup>4</sup>?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of squares = (Sum)2 − 2(Product) = 102 − 2(4) = 92

Sum of 4th powers = (Sum of squares)2 − 2(Product)2

⇒ 922 − 2(42) = 8464 − 32 = 8432

∴ The correct answer is 8432.

Alternate Method

Given:

x + y = 10

xy = 4

Formula Used:

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

Calculations:

⇒ (x + y)2 = 102

⇒ x2 + y2 + 2xy = 100

⇒ x2 + y2 + 2(4) = 100

⇒ x2 + y2 = 100 − 8 = 92

⇒ (x2 + y2)2 = 922

⇒ x4 + y4 + 2x2y2 = 8464

⇒ x4 + y4 + 2(xy)2 = 8464

⇒ x4 + y4 + 2(4)2 = 8464

⇒ x4 + y4 + 32 = 8464

⇒ x4 + y4 = 8464 − 32

⇒ x4 + y4 = 8432

∴ The correct answer is 8432.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for Squares

The identity (x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy can be rearranged as x2 + y2 = (x + y)2 − 2xy to find the sum of squares of two variables.

Higher Order Power Sums

To find x4 + y4, we treat x2 and y2 as the variables and apply the same logic: x4 + y4 = (x2 + y2)2 − 2(xy)2.

Sum of Cubes

Similarly, the sum of cubes can be found using the identity x3 + y3 = (x + y)(x2 − xy + y2) or (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y).

questions.question: M is the largest three digit number which when divided by 6 and 5 leaves remainder 5 and 3 respectively. What will be the remainder when M is divided by 11?
questions.questionHtml: M is the largest three digit number which when divided by 6 and 5 leaves remainder 5 and 3 respectively. What will be the remainder when M is divided by 11?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

First number satisfying M ≡ 5 (mod 6) and M ≡ 3 (mod 5) is 23.

General form of M = LCM(6, 5) × k + 23 = 30k + 23.

For largest 3-digit number, 30k + 23 ≤ 999 ⇒ 30k ≤ 976 ⇒ k = 32.

Largest number M = (30 × 32) + 23 = 960 + 23 = 983.

Remainder when 983 is divided by 11 = 983 − (11 × 89) = 4.

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

Divisor 1 (d1) = 6, Remainder 1 (r1) = 5

Divisor 2 (d2) = 5, Remainder 2 (r2) = 3

Formula:

Number (M) = LCM(d1, d2) × k + First common value

Finding the first common number:

Multiples of 6 + 5: 5, 11, 17, 23, 29...

Multiples of 5 + 3: 3, 8, 13, 18, 23, 28...

⇒ Common value = 23

⇒ LCM(6, 5) = 30

⇒ General form M = 30k + 23

⇒ For largest 3-digit number, 30k + 23 < 1000

⇒ 30k < 977 ⇒ k = 32

⇒ M = (30 × 32) + 23 = 960 + 23 = 983

Division by 11:

⇒ 983 ÷ 11

⇒ 11 × 80 = 880

⇒ 11 × 9 = 99

⇒ Total quotient = 89, Product = 979

⇒ Remainder = 983 − 979 = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11. For 983: (9+3) − 8 = 4.

Chinese Remainder Theorem (Simplified)

For a system of linear congruences with coprime moduli m1, m2, the solution is unique modulo (m1 × m2).

LCM of Numbers

LCM(a, b) is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by both a and b. If a and b are coprime, LCM = a × b.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE? I. √5 + √5 > √7 + √3 II. √6 + √7 > √8 + √5 III. √3 + √9 > √6 + √6
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

I. √5 + √5 > √7 + √3

II. √6 + √7 > √8 + √5

III. √3 + √9 > √6 + √6
questions.solution:
Given:

I. √5 + √5 > √7 + √3

II. √6 + √7 > √8 + √5

III. √3 + √9 > √6 + √6

Formula used:

(√a + √b)2 = a + b + 2√(a × b)

If (a + b) is constant, then (√a + √b) is greater when (a × b) is greater.

Calculations:

For I: 5 + 5 = 10 and 7 + 3 = 10

⇒ \((\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{5})^2 = 10 + 2\sqrt{25}\)

⇒ \((\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})^2 = 10 + 2\sqrt{21}\)

⇒ 25 > 21 (True)

For II: 6 + 7 = 13 and 8 + 5 = 13

⇒ \((\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{7})^2 = 13 + 2\sqrt{42}\)

⇒ \((\sqrt{8} + \sqrt{5})^2 = 13 + 2\sqrt{40}\)

⇒ 42 > 40 (True)

For III: 3 + 9 = 12 and 6 + 6 = 12

⇒ \((\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{9})^2 = 12 + 2\sqrt{27}\)

⇒ \((\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{6})^2 = 12 + 2\sqrt{36}\)

⇒ 27 < 36 (False)

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: If, \({\rm{a}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 + \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 3 - \sqrt 2 }}\:{\rm{and\;b}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 3 + \sqrt 2 }}\) , then what is the value of a 2 + b 2 - ab?
questions.questionHtml: If, \({\rm{a}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 + \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 3 - \sqrt 2 }}\:{\rm{and\;b}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 3 + \sqrt 2 }}\), then what is the value of a2 + b2 - ab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 97
Key Points
  • Given values: a = (√3 + √2) / (√3 − √2) and b = (√3 − √2) / (√3 + √2).
  • To find the value of a2 + b2 − ab, we first simplify the expressions for a and b by rationalizing the denominator.
  • Rationalizing a:
    a = [(√3 + √2) × (√3 + √2)] / [(√3 − √2) × (√3 + √2)]
    a = (√3 + √2)2 / [(√3)2 − (√2)2]
    a = (3 + 2 + 2√6) / (3 − 2)
    a = 5 + 2√6
  • Rationalizing b:
    b = [(√3 − √2) × (√3 − √2)] / [(√3 + √2) × (√3 − √2)]
    b = (√3 − √2)2 / [(√3)2 − (√2)2]
    b = (3 + 2 − 2√6) / (3 − 2)
    b = 5 − 2√6
  • Calculate (a + b) and (ab):
    a + b = (5 + 2√6) + (5 − 2√6) = 10
    ab = [( √3 + √2 ) / ( √3 − √2 )] × [( √3 − √2 ) / ( √3 + √2 )] = 1
  • Using the algebraic identity:
    a2 + b2 − ab = (a + b)2 − 2ab − ab
    a2 + b2 − ab = (a + b)2 − 3ab
  • Substituting the values:
    Value = (10)2 − 3(1)
    Value = 100 − 3 = 97.
  • Therefore, the correct value is 97.
Additional Information
  • Rationalization is a process used to eliminate radicals (like square roots) from the denominator of a fraction by multiplying the numerator and denominator by a suitable conjugate.
  • The Conjugate of (x − y) is (x + y), and their product results in a difference of squares: (x − y)(x + y) = x2 − y2.
  • Useful identities for such problems include:
    1. (x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy
    2. (x − y)2 = x2 + y2 − 2xy
    3. x2 + y2 = (x + y)2 − 2xy
  • In this specific case, a and b are reciprocals of each other (a = 1/b), which simplifies the term ab to 1.

questions.question: If the difference between the roots of the equation Ax 2 - Bx + C = 0 is 4, then which of the following is TRUE?
questions.questionHtml: If the difference between the roots of the equation Ax<sup>2</sup> - Bx + C = 0 is 4, then which of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For Ax2 − Bx + C = 0, the difference of roots is √D/|A|.

Given difference = 4, so √(B2 − 4AC) / A = 4.

Squaring both sides: (B2 − 4AC) / A2 = 16 ⇒ B2 − 4AC = 16A2.

Rearranging the terms: B2 − 16A2 = 4AC.

Check options: B2 − 10A2 = 4AC + 6A2 simplifies to B2 − 16A2 = 4AC.

∴ The correct answer is B2 − 10A2 = 4AC + 6A2.

Alternate Method

Given: Quadratic equation Ax2 − Bx + C = 0 and difference of roots |α − β| = 4.

Formula Used:

Sum of roots (α + β) = −b/a = −(−B)/A = B/A

Product of roots (αβ) = c/a = C/A

Identity: (α − β)2 = (α + β)2 − 4αβ

Calculations:

⇒ (α − β) = 4

⇒ (α − β)2 = 42 = 16

⇒ (B/A)2 − 4(C/A) = 16

⇒ B2/A2 − 4C/A = 16

⇒ (B2 − 4AC) / A2 = 16

⇒ B2 − 4AC = 16A2

⇒ B2 − 16A2 = 4AC

Now, let us verify Option 2:

⇒ B2 − 10A2 = 4AC + 6A2

⇒ B2 − 10A2 − 6A2 = 4AC

⇒ B2 − 16A2 = 4AC

This matches our derived condition.

∴ The correct answer is B2 − 10A2 = 4AC + 6A2.

Additional Information

Nature of Roots

For ax2 + bx + c = 0, the discriminant D = b2 − 4ac determines root nature: D > 0 (real and distinct), D = 0 (real and equal), D < 0 (imaginary).

Sum and Product of Roots

For a quadratic equation, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.

Relation between Roots

The difference of roots |α − β| can always be expressed as √D/|a|.

questions.question: α and β are the roots of the quadratic equation. If α + β = 8 and α - β = 2√5, then which of the following equation will have roots α 4 and β 4 ?
questions.questionHtml: α and β are the roots of the quadratic equation. If α + β = 8 and α - β = 2√5, then which of the following equation will have roots α<sup>4</sup> and β<sup>4</sup>?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Product of roots αβ = [(α + β)2 − (α − β)2] ÷ 4 = [82 − (2√5)2] ÷ 4 = (64 − 20) ÷ 4 = 11.

Product of new roots = (αβ)4 = 114 = 14641.

α2 + β2 = (α + β)2 − 2αβ = 64 − 2(11) = 42.

Sum of new roots (α4 + β4) = (α2 + β2)2 − 2(αβ)2 = 422 − 2(11)2 = 1764 − 242 = 1522.

The required equation is x2 − (Sum)x + (Product) = 0 ⇒ x2 − 1522x + 14641 = 0.

∴ The correct answer is x2 − 1522x + 14641 = 0.

Given: α + β = 8 and α − β = 2√5

Method: Solve for α and β then find α4 and β4.

⇒ Adding the equations: 2α = 8 + 2√5 ⇒ α = 4 + √5

⇒ Subtracting the equations: 2β = 8 − 2√5 ⇒ β = 4 − √5

⇒ α2 = (4 + √5)2 = 16 + 5 + 8√5 = 21 + 8√5

⇒ β2 = (4 − √5)2 = 16 + 5 − 8√5 = 21 − 8√5

⇒ New Sum (S) = α4 + β4 = (α2)2 + (β2)2

⇒ S = (21 + 8√5)2 + (21 − 8√5)2

⇒ S = 2 × (212 + (8√5)2) = 2 × (441 + 320) = 2 × 761 = 1522

⇒ New Product (P) = α4 × β4 = (αβ)4

⇒ αβ = (4 + √5)(4 − √5) = 16 − 5 = 11

⇒ P = 114 = 14641

⇒ Quadratic Equation: x2 − Sx + P = 0 ⇒ x2 − 1522x + 14641 = 0

∴ The correct answer is x2 − 1522x + 14641 = 0.

Additional Information

Sum and Product of Roots

α2 + β2 = (α + β)2 − 2αβ. Further, α4 + β4 = (α2 + β2)2 − 2(αβ)2.

questions.question: If a and b are the roots of the equation Px 2 - Qx + R = 0, then what is the value of (1/a 2 ) + (1/b 2 ) + (a/b) + (b/a)?
questions.questionHtml: If a and b are the roots of the equation Px<sup>2</sup> - Qx + R = 0, then what is the value of (1/a<sup>2</sup>) + (1/b<sup>2</sup>) + (a/b) + (b/a)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For equation Px2 − Qx + R = 0, sum (a+b) = Q/P and product (ab) = R/P.

Expression = (1/a2 + 1/b2) + (a/b + b/a) = (a2+b2)/(ab)2 + (a2+b2)/ab.

Substitute a2+b2 = (a+b)2 − 2ab = (Q/P)2 − 2(R/P) = (Q2 − 2PR)/P2.

Expression = [(Q2 − 2PR)/P2] × [P2/R2 + P/R] = [(Q2 − 2PR)/P2] × [P(P+R)/R2].

Expression = (Q2 − 2PR)(P + R) / (PR2).

∴ The correct answer is (Q2 − 2PR)(R + P) / PR2.

Alternate Method

Given Quadratic Equation: Px2 − Qx + R = 0

Roots of the equation are a and b.

Formula used: Sum of roots = − (coefficient of x) / (coefficient of x2) | Product of roots = constant term / (coefficient of x2)

⇒ Sum of roots (a + b) = −(−Q) / P = Q / P

⇒ Product of roots (ab) = R / P

⇒ Calculate (a2 + b2) = (a + b)2 − 2ab

⇒ a2 + b2 = (Q/P)2 − 2(R/P) = (Q2 / P2) − (2R / P) = (Q2 − 2PR) / P2

⇒ Target expression: (1/a2) + (1/b2) + (a/b) + (b/a)

⇒ [ (a2 + b2) / (ab)2 ] + [ (a2 + b2) / (ab) ]

⇒ (a2 + b2) × [ 1/(ab)2 + 1/(ab) ]

⇒ [ (Q2 − 2PR) / P2 ] × [ 1 / (R/P)2 + 1 / (R/P) ]

⇒ [ (Q2 − 2PR) / P2 ] × [ P2/R2 + P/R ]

⇒ [ (Q2 − 2PR) / P2 ] × [ (P2 + PR) / R2 ]

⇒ [ (Q2 − 2PR) / P2 ] × [ P(P + R) / R2 ]

⇒ [ (Q2 − 2PR) (P + R) ] / (P × R2)

∴ The correct answer is (Q2 − 2PR)(R + P) / PR2.

Additional Information

Nature of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0, the nature of roots depends on the discriminant D = b2 − 4ac. If D > 0 roots are real and distinct, if D = 0 roots are real and equal, and if D < 0 roots are imaginary.

The sum of roots (α + β) is equal to −b/a and the product of roots (αβ) is equal to c/a.

Formation of Quadratic Equation

If the roots are given as α and β, the equation is formed by x2 − (α + β)x + (αβ) = 0.

questions.question: If x 2 - 16x + 59 = 0, then what is the value of (x - 6) 2 + [1/(x - 6) 2 ]?
questions.questionHtml: If x<sup>2</sup> - 16x + 59 = 0, then what is the value of (x - 6)<sup>2</sup> + [1/(x - 6)<sup>2</sup>]?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let a = x − 6, then x = a + 6.

Substitute into x2 − 16x + 59 = 0 ⇒ (a + 6)2 − 16(a + 6) + 59 = 0.

Expanding: a2 + 12a + 36 − 16a − 96 + 59 = 0 ⇒ a2 − 4a − 1 = 0.

Divide by a: a − 4 − 1/a = 0 ⇒ a − 1/a = 4.

Required value: a2 + 1/a2 = (a − 1/a)2 + 2 = 42 + 2 = 18.

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Alternate Method

Given: x2 − 16x + 59 = 0

Formula Used: (a − b)2 = a2 + b2 − 2ab; If k − 1/k = n, then k2 + 1/k2 = n2 + 2

⇒ Let k = x − 6

⇒ x = k + 6

⇒ Substitute x in the given equation: (k + 6)2 − 16(k + 6) + 59 = 0

⇒ k2 + 12k + 36 − 16k − 96 + 59 = 0

⇒ k2 − 4k − 1 = 0

⇒ Dividing the entire equation by k: k − 4 − 1/k = 0

⇒ k − 1/k = 4

⇒ Squaring both sides: (k − 1/k)2 = 42

⇒ k2 + 1/k2 − 2 = 16

⇒ k2 + 1/k2 = 16 + 2

⇒ (x − 6)2 + 1/(x − 6)2 = 18

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Additional Information

Algebraic Reciprocal Identities

For any variable k, if k + 1/k = n, then k2 + 1/k2 = n2 − 2. If k − 1/k = n, then k2 + 1/k2 = n2 + 2.

questions.question: If A and B are the roots of the equation Ax 2 - A 2 x + AB = 0, then what is the value of A and B respectively?
questions.questionHtml: If A and B are the roots of the equation Ax<sup>2</sup> - A<sup>2</sup>x + AB = 0, then what is the value of A and B respectively?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For Ax2 − A2x + AB = 0, Sum of roots = −(−A2)/A = A.

Given roots are A and B, so Sum = A + B.

Equating: A + B = A ⇒ B = 0.

Product of roots = AB/A = B. Given product A × B = B is satisfied for B = 0.

Checking options, only (1, 0) satisfies B = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 1, 0.

Alternate Method

Given: Quadratic Equation Ax2 − A2x + AB = 0 where A and B are the roots.

Formula: For a quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0, Sum of roots = −b/a and Product of roots = c/a.

⇒ Comparing with standard form: a = A, b = −A2, c = AB.

⇒ Sum of roots = α + β = −(−A2) / A = A.

⇒ Given roots are A and B, so A + B = A.

⇒ A + B = A ⇒ B = 0.

⇒ Product of roots = α × β = AB / A = B.

⇒ Given roots product = A × B.

⇒ A × B = B ⇒ B(A − 1) = 0.

⇒ Substituting B = 0 in the product equation: 0(A − 1) = 0, which is true for any A ≠ 0.

⇒ From the given options, the pair that matches B = 0 is A = 1 and B = 0.

⇒ Verification: If A = 1 and B = 0, the equation becomes 1x2 − (1)2x + (1 × 0) = 0 → x2 − x = 0, which gives roots x = 0 and x = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1, 0.

Additional Information

Sum and Product of Roots

For any quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0, the roots α and β satisfy α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a.

Formation of Quadratic Equation

If the roots are known, the equation is given by x2 − (Sum of roots)x + (Product of roots) = 0.

Nature of Roots

The discriminant D = b2 − 4ac determines if roots are real and distinct (D > 0), real and equal (D = 0), or imaginary (D < 0).

questions.question: α and β are the roots of the quadratic equation x 2 - x - 1 = 0. What is the value of α 8 + β 8 ?
questions.questionHtml: α and β are the roots of the quadratic equation x<sup>2</sup> - x - 1 = 0. What is the value of α<sup>8</sup> + β<sup>8</sup>?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For x2 − x − 1 = 0, Sum (S) = 1 and Product (P) = −1.

Using recursive doubling: S2 = S2 − 2P = 12 − 2(−1) = 3.

Next power: S4 = S22 − 2P2 = 32 − 2(1) = 7.

Required power: S8 = S42 − 2P4 = 72 − 2(1) = 47.

∴ The correct answer is 47.

Alternate Method

Given: Equation x2 − x − 1 = 0 with roots α and β.

Formula Used: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a.

⇒ α + β = −(−1)/1 = 1

⇒ αβ = −1/1 = −1

⇒ α2 + β2 = (α + β)2 − 2αβ = (1)2 − 2(−1) = 3

⇒ α4 + β4 = (α2 + β2)2 − 2(αβ)2 = (3)2 − 2(−1)2 = 9 − 2 = 7

⇒ α8 + β8 = (α4 + β4)2 − 2(αβ)4 = (7)2 − 2(−1)4 = 49 − 2 = 47

∴ The correct answer is 47.

Additional Information

Sum and Product of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots α + β = −b/a and the product αβ = c/a.

Newton’s Sums for Roots

If Sn = αn + βn for the equation x2 − px + q = 0, then Sn = pSn−1 − qSn−2.

questions.question: If a + b + c = 9, ab + bc + ca = 26, a 3 + b 3 = 91, b 3 + c 3 = 72 and c 3 + a 3 = 35, then what is the value of abc?
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c = 9, ab + bc + ca = 26, a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> = 91, b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3</sup> = 72 and c<sup>3</sup> + a<sup>3</sup> = 35, then what is the value of abc?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By observing the given cube sums: a3 + c3 = 35 → 27 + 8 → 33 + 23

And b3 + c3 = 72 → 64 + 8 → 43 + 23

Checking these values: a = 3, b = 4, c = 2

Verification: a + b + c = 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 (Satisfied)

Product: abc = 3 × 4 × 2 = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Alternate Method

Given: a + b + c = 9, ab + bc + ca = 26

Summing the three cube equations:

⇒ (a3 + b3) + (b3 + c3) + (c3 + a3) = 91 + 72 + 35

⇒ 2(a3 + b3 + c3) = 198

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 = 99

Using the algebraic identity: a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)((a + b + c)2 − 3(ab + bc + ca))

⇒ 99 − 3abc = 9 × (92 − 3 × 26)

⇒ 99 − 3abc = 9 × (81 − 78)

⇒ 99 − 3abc = 9 × 3

⇒ 99 − 3abc = 27

⇒ 3abc = 99 − 27 = 72

⇒ abc = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

The identity a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ca) is fundamental for solving three-variable problems.

Square of a Trinomial

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca). This relates the sum, the sum of squares, and the sum of products taken two at a time.

Special Conditional Case

If a + b + c = 0, then the identity simplifies to a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

questions.question: If x 3 – 4x 2 + 19 = 6(x – 1), then what is the value of [x 2 + {1/(x – 4)}]?
questions.questionHtml: If x<sup>3</sup> – 4x<sup>2</sup> + 19 = 6(x – 1), then what is the value of [x<sup>2</sup> + {1/(x – 4)}]?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given equation: x3 − 4x2 + 19 = 6x − 6

Factorize the left side to include (x − 4): x2(x − 4) + 19 = 6x − 6

Rearrange: x2(x − 4) = 6x − 25 ⇒ x2(x − 4) = 6(x − 4) − 1

Divide both sides by (x − 4): x2 = 6 − 1/(x − 4)

Result: x2 + 1/(x − 4) = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given: x3 − 4x2 + 19 = 6(x − 1)

Formula Used: Algebraic manipulation and division by common terms.

⇒ x3 − 4x2 + 19 = 6x − 6

⇒ x2(x − 4) + 19 = 6x − 6

⇒ x2(x − 4) = 6x − 6 − 19

⇒ x2(x − 4) = 6x − 25

⇒ x2 = (6x − 25) / (x − 4)

⇒ x2 = [6(x − 4) − 24 + 24 − 25] / (x − 4)

⇒ x2 = [6(x − 4) − 1] / (x − 4)

⇒ x2 = 6 − 1/(x − 4)

⇒ x2 + 1/(x − 4) = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities

Standard identities like (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2 and (a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b) are essential for simplifying complex polynomial expressions.

Remainder Theorem

If a polynomial f(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is equal to f(a). This is useful for checking factors or simplifying rational expressions.

Division Algorithm

For any polynomial division, Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. This relationship helps in isolating specific algebraic terms.

questions.question: Cost of 8 pencils, 5 pens and 3 erasers is Rs. 111. Cost of 9 pencils, 6 pens and 5 erasers is Rs. 130. Cost of 16 pencils, 11 pens and 3 erasers is Rs. 221. What is the cost (in Rs) of 39 pencils, 26 pens and 13 erasers?
questions.questionHtml: Cost of 8 pencils, 5 pens and 3 erasers is Rs. 111. Cost of 9 pencils, 6 pens and 5 erasers is Rs. 130. Cost of 16 pencils, 11 pens and 3 erasers is Rs. 221. What is the cost (in Rs) of 39 pencils, 26 pens and 13 erasers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Observe the combined total: Summing all three equations gives 33 Pencils + 22 Pens + 11 Erasers = 111 + 130 + 221 = 462.

Find the cost of a base unit (3 Pencils + 2 Pens + 1 Eraser) by dividing the total by 11: 462 ÷ 11 = 42.

The target quantity (39 Pencils, 26 Pens, 13 Erasers) is exactly 13 times the base unit.

Required cost = 13 × 42 = 546.

∴ The correct answer is ₹546.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of 8 Pencils + 5 Pens + 3 Erasers = ₹111

Cost of 9 Pencils + 6 Pens + 5 Erasers = ₹130

Cost of 16 Pencils + 11 Pens + 3 Erasers = ₹221

Formula Used:

Total Cost = (Cost per Pencil × Quantity) + (Cost per Pen × Quantity) + (Cost per Eraser × Quantity)

Calculations:

⇒ Let P, N, and E be the cost of one pencil, one pen, and one eraser respectively.

⇒ Eq.1: 8P + 5N + 3E = 111

⇒ Eq.2: 9P + 6N + 5E = 130

⇒ Eq.3: 16P + 11N + 3E = 221

⇒ Adding all three equations: (8 + 9 + 16)P + (5 + 6 + 11)N + (3 + 5 + 3)E = 111 + 130 + 221

⇒ 33P + 22N + 11E = 462

⇒ Divide the entire equation by 11: 3P + 2N + E = 462 ÷ 11 = 42

⇒ We need the cost of 39P + 26N + 13E.

⇒ Target cost = 13 × (3P + 2N + E)

⇒ Target cost = 13 × 42 = 546.

∴ The correct answer is ₹546.

Additional Information

Linear Equations in Three Variables

A system of the form ax + by + cz = d, which can be solved using elimination, substitution, or Cramer’s Rule.

Summation Technique

When the required expression is a multiple of the sum of the given equations, add them directly to avoid calculating individual variable values.
